questions.stem: Suppose your school is organizing an orientation program to help the freshmen adapt to the new environment and academic studies. You are now to write a proposal, which may include its aim, duration, participants and activities. You will have 30 minutes to write the proposal. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
A Proposal for the Freshmen Orientation Program

Our school is planning an orientation program for this year's freshmen, and its main arrangements are proposed below. The program aims to help new students adapt to the new environment and academic studies as smoothly and quickly as possible.

In terms of duration, the program will last for one week, starting from the day of registration. As for the participants, it is open to all incoming freshmen, and it will be organized by the Student Union together with volunteer seniors and several advisers from each department.

A variety of activities will be arranged during the week. First, campus tours and library workshops will help newcomers find their way around. Second, group meetings with academic advisers will introduce course selection and effective study methods. Finally, evening social parties will give students a chance to make new friends and relax.

We are confident that this program will give every freshman a warm and confident start. Your approval and support would be highly appreciated.

The Student Union

sections.title: Section II Listening Comprehension
sections.note: 听力为历年真题原文，题目与答案为官方标准答案；在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: United Airlines has apologised for mistakenly shipping an American family's pet dog thousands of miles in the wrong direction to Japan.
transcript.zh: 美国联合航空公司为误将一个美国家庭的宠物狗运送到数千英里外的日本方向而道歉。

transcript.text: The dog owner's beloved 10-year-old dog named Buddy took an unexpected 16-hour flight to Tokyo following a mix-up by the airline.
transcript.zh: 狗主人心爱的10岁狗狗名叫Buddy,由于航空公司的失误,意外搭乘了16小时的航班飞往东京。

transcript.text: The dog owner's family are currently in the process of moving. They were meant to be reunited with the pet in their new home city in Texas.
transcript.zh: 狗主人一家目前正在搬家过程中。他们原本应该在得克萨斯州的新家与宠物团聚。

transcript.text: But when they arrived at the United Airlines cargo facility in the southern U.S. state, they found a stranger's dog waiting in Buddy's place.
transcript.zh: 但当他们到达美国南部州的美国联合航空公司货运设施时,发现一只陌生的狗在Buddy的位置等待。

transcript.text: Both of the dogs had been sent to the wrong destinations on connecting flights from Denver, with Buddy mistakenly being sent to Japan instead.
transcript.zh: 这两只狗都在丹佛转机时被送到了错误的目的地, Buddy被错误地送到了日本。

transcript.text: Buddy was given a physical checkup when he arrived at Tokyo's International Airport. The dog was then sent back to the U.S. on a private charter jet.
transcript.zh: Buddy抵达东京国际机场后接受了身体检查。随后这只狗被用私人包机送回美国。

transcript.text: "I'm so glad he's alive and coming home soon!" said the relieved dog owner.
transcript.zh: "我太高兴了,它还活着并且很快就要回家了!"如释重负的狗主人说。

transcript.text: "And an error occurred during the connections in Denver. We have notified our customers that their pets arrived safely. We will arrange to return the pets to them as soon as possible," a spokesperson of United Airlines said.
transcript.zh: "在丹佛转机期间发生了一个错误。我们已通知客户他们的宠物安全抵达。我们将尽快安排将宠物送还给他们。"美国联合航空公司发言人表示。

questions.stem: What does the news report say about United Airlines?

options.text: It found a pet dog on board a plane to a city in Texas.
It had one of its cargo planes land at a wrong airport.
It sent two dogs to the wrong destinations.
It had two of its domestic flights mixed up.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P5）：Both of the dogs had been sent to the wrong destinations on connecting flights from Denver, with Buddy mistakenly being sent to Japan instead.信号：Both…wrong destinations 直陈事故 。这句以 Both of the dogs had been sent to the wrong destinations 正面点出事故核心——两只狗都被送错…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项盗用了原文里 Texas 这个地名（their new home city in Texas），但原文是说一家人本应在得州的新家与狗团聚，并非『在飞往得州的飞机上发现一只狗』；它把真实情节拼凑改写，属听到 Texas 就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：United Airlines has apologised for mistakenly shipping an American family's pet dog thousands of miles in the wrong direction
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：原文反复说送错的是 dog（shipping an American family's pet dog…in the wrong direction），是『狗被运错方向』，从没说『一架货机降错机场』；选项把错送对象从狗偷换成 cargo plane、把『送错目的地』偷换成『降错机场』，与原文不符。 借用原文：Both of the dogs had been sent to the wrong destinations on connecting flights from Denver
optionAnalysis.D: 答非所问：原文是两只狗在转机时被送错（on connecting flights from Denver），出错的是狗的去向；选项却说是『两个国内航班被搞混』，把出错对象从狗换成 flights，且原文只字未提『国内航班搞混』，属答非所问。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（Both of the dogs had been sent to the wrong destinations ↔ It sent two dogs to the wrong destinations. Both the dogs = two dogs）

questions.evidenceText: Both of the dogs had been sent to the wrong destinations on connecting flights from Denver, with Buddy mistakenly being sent to Japan instead.

questions.stem: What did the spokesperson for United Airlines say they would do after the incident?

options.text: Correct their mistake as soon as possible.
Give the two pets a physical checkup.
Hire a charter jet to bring the pets back.
Send another plane to continue the flight.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P8）：We will arrange to return the pets to them as soon as possible.信号：We will 未来承诺 。这句出自发言人原话，以 We will arrange to return the pets to them as soon as possible 的 We will 领头，是典型的官方…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项盗用了原文真出现的 physical checkup（Buddy was given a physical checkup），但那是 Buddy 到东京后已经做过的事，不是发言人承诺『事故后将要做』的动作；时间错位，张冠李戴到发言人头上。 借用原文：The dog was then sent back to the U.S. on a private charter jet.
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项盗用原文的 charter jet（sent back to the U.S. on a private charter jet），但那是叙述 Buddy 已经被私人包机送回美国的既成事实，不是发言人对今后的承诺；选项把已发生说成将要做，且 Hire（雇用）也非原文所述。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：原文从没说要『再派一架飞机继续这趟飞行』；发言人只承诺尽快把宠物送还（return the pets to them as soon as possible）。选项 Send another plane to continue the flight. 是凭 plane/flight 这类话题词臆造的动作，未提及。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（We will arrange to return the pets to them as soon as possible ↔ Correct their mistake as soon as possible. 送还宠物=纠正错误）

questions.evidenceText: We will arrange to return the pets to them as soon as possible.

transcript.text: Officials at Reid Park Zoo in Tucson Arizona are celebrating the birth of a baby elephant. Zoo officials say the baby was born on Monday. It is a female and she weighs nearly 130 kilograms.
transcript.zh: 亚利桑那州图森市Reid Park动物园的官员们正在庆祝一头小象的诞生。动物园官员表示,这头小象于周一出生。它是雌性,体重近130公斤。

transcript.text: Semba, her mother, is a 30-year-old African elephant. The pregnancy lasted 22 months.
transcript.zh: 它的母亲Semba是一头30岁的非洲象。怀孕期持续了22个月。

transcript.text: Officials describe the baby elephant as "healthy, standing and nursing".
transcript.zh: 官员们描述这头小象"健康、能站立并在哺乳"。

transcript.text: The baby hasn't been given a name yet.
transcript.zh: 这头小象还没有被命名。

transcript.text: Semba has given birth before. Zoo officials said during this pregnancy, she was closely monitored through physical exams and blood tests.
transcript.zh: Semba之前曾生育过。动物园官员表示,在这次怀孕期间,通过身体检查和血液测试对她进行了密切监测。

transcript.text: Dr. Sue Tygielski is the zoo's director of zoological operations. She said the elephant's birth went smoothly and that there were no complications.
transcript.zh: Sue Tygielski博士是该动物园的动物运营总监。她表示大象的分娩过程顺利,没有出现并发症。

transcript.text: The new baby expands the zoo's elephant herd to six. That includes the baby's parents, a sister, a brother and an adult female.
transcript.zh: 这头新生小象使动物园的大象群扩大到六头。其中包括小象的父母、一个姐姐、一个哥哥和一头成年雌象。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the mother elephant Semba?

options.text: She has a big family of six.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P5）：Semba has given birth before.信号：直陈母象过往经历 。答案句是录音里专门交代 Semba 经历的一句 Semba has given birth before.，它直接陈述了关于这只母象本身的一项事实，与题干 "关于 Semba 我们了解到什么" 严…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 She weighs 130 kilograms. 盗用了录音里真实出现的数字 130 公斤，但录音说的是新生小象 she weighs nearly 130 kilograms，主语是 baby 而非母亲 Semba，把宝宝的体重安到了母亲头上，对象搞错。 借用原文：a 30-year-old African elephant
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：选项 She was brought from Africa. 借用了录音里的 Africa 一词，但录音只说 Semba, her mother, is a 30-year-old African elephant.——她是一头 "非洲象"（品种），并没有说 "她是从非洲被带来的"，把物种来源偷换成了运输来历。 借用原文：expands the zoo's elephant herd to six
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：选项 She has a big family of six. 盗用了录音末尾的数字 six，但录音说 The new baby expands the zoo's elephant herd to six.——是 "动物园象群扩大到六只"，描述的是整个园区象群规模，而非 "母亲 Semba 有一个六口之家"，对象与口径都被改了。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（has given birth before ↔ has had babies before 生过=有过孩子）

questions.evidenceText: Semba has given birth before.

questions.stem: What does the report say about the birth of the new baby elephant?

options.text: It was monitored by Dr. Sue Tygielski.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：She said the elephant's birth went smoothly and that there were no complications.信号：对出生过程的直接定性 。答案句 the elephant's birth went smoothly and that there were no complications 是录音里唯一对 "出生过程怎么样" 下定…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 It took 22 hours. 盗用了数字 22，但录音里的 22 是 The pregnancy lasted 22 months.——是怀孕 22 个 "月"，且说的是孕期长短不是 "出生过程用了多久"，单位（hours↔months）和对象（出生过程↔整个孕期）双双被换。 借用原文：there were no complications
optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：选项 It had some complications. 直接盗用录音原词 complications，但录音是 there were no complications——明确说 "没有" 并发症，选项却说 "有一些"，把否定改成了肯定，极性正好相反。 借用原文：during this pregnancy, she was closely monitored
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：选项 It was monitored by Dr. Sue Tygielski. 把录音里真实出现的人名 Sue Tygielski 搬来当出生过程的监控者，但录音说被密切监控的是 during this pregnancy, she was closely monitored——监控的是 Semba 的 "孕期"，而 Tygielski 博士只是在 Dr. Sue Tygielski is the zoo's director 里被介绍头衔并转述 "出生很顺利"，并没说出生由她监控，把 "孕期被监控" 和 "这位博士" 硬拼到一起。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（went smoothly ↔ It was smooth. 副词转形容词同义）

questions.evidenceText: She said the elephant's birth went smoothly and that there were no complications.

transcript.text: Three years ago, a couple was enjoying a meal at a beach restaurant. The restaurant was built on a wooden structure above the sea-water. During the meal, the man's wedding ring slipped off his finger. It fell through the wooden floorboards, apparently lost forever.
transcript.zh: 三年前,一对夫妇在一家海滩餐厅用餐。这家餐厅建在海面上的木质结构上。用餐期间,男士的结婚戒指从手指上滑落了。它掉进了木地板的缝隙里,看似永远丢失了。

transcript.text: Recently, the restaurant manager Ryan Krivoy decided to replace the wooden deck and he found an old gold coin, some $100 bills and a silver wedding ring while replacing the deck.
transcript.zh: 最近,餐厅经理Ryan Krivoy决定更换木质甲板,在更换甲板时他发现了一枚古老的金币、一些100美元的钞票和一枚银质结婚戒指。

transcript.text: The restaurant waitress Sasha Formica posted a picture of the ring on Facebook. The post was shared about 5,000 times.
transcript.zh: 餐厅女服务员Sasha Formica在Facebook上发布了这枚戒指的照片。这条帖子被分享了大约5000次。

transcript.text: Three days later, the happy wife called to claim the ring. She even texted pictures of her and her husband eating there in 2017 as proof.
transcript.zh: 三天后,这位高兴的妻子打电话来认领戒指。她甚至发送了她和丈夫2017年在那里用餐的照片作为证明。

transcript.text: The restaurant mailed the ring back to the happy couple. Meanwhile, Krivoy discovered that the gold coin was very rare. It was from 1855 and worth as much as $2,000.
transcript.zh: 餐厅将戒指邮寄回给了这对幸福的夫妇。与此同时, Krivoy发现那枚金币非常罕见。它来自1855年,价值高达2000美元。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the restaurant?

options.text: It started business three years ago.
It was built above the sea-water.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：The restaurant was built on a wooden structure above the sea-water.信号：录音里唯一直接描述餐厅本身的句子 。全篇只有这一句在正面描述餐厅这个事物本身——The restaurant was built on a wooden structure above the sea-water.，…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：It enjoyed great popularity. 说餐厅很受欢迎，但录音通篇只讲戒指失而复得，从未评价餐厅的人气或生意好坏，属于无中生有。
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：It started business three years ago. 借了录音开头的 three years ago，但 Three years ago, a couple was enjoying a meal 里这个时间是指三年前有对夫妇在此用餐、戒指掉落，根本不是讲餐厅三年前开业；把三年前从用餐时间偷换成开业时间，是典型的原词陷阱。 借用原文：a couple was enjoying a meal at a beach restaurant
optionAnalysis.C: 过度推断：It was frequented by newly-weds. 说餐厅常被新婚夫妇光顾；录音只提到一对夫妇曾来用餐 a couple was enjoying a meal，既没说他们是新婚、更没说这里常有新婚夫妇来，属于由一对夫妇过度推断成常客群体。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（built on a wooden structure above the sea-water ↔ It was built above the sea-water. 选项是原句的压缩概括）

questions.evidenceText: The restaurant was built on a wooden structure above the sea-water.

questions.stem: What did the restaurant manager decide to do recently?

options.text: Expand his business on the beach.
Post a picture of his restaurant online.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：Recently, the restaurant manager Ryan Krivoy decided to replace the wooden deck and he found an old gold coin, some $100 bills and a silver wedding ring while replacing the deck.信号：decided to 直接给出经理的决定动作 。the restaurant manager Ryan Krivoy decided to replace the wooden deck 里 decided to 后…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：Expand his business on the beach. 里的 beach 借自录音背景中的海边餐厅（beach restaurant），但录音从没说经理要扩张生意，他决定的是换平台 replace the wooden deck；把场景词 beach 拿来拼一个原文没有的动作，是原词陷阱加无中生有。 借用原文：The restaurant waitress Sasha Formica posted a picture of the ring on Facebook.
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：Post a picture of his restaurant online. 里发照片到网上这件事，录音里做的人是女服务员 The restaurant waitress Sasha Formica posted a picture of the ring on Facebook.，且发的是戒指照片不是餐厅照片；既把动作的人从服务员张冠李戴到经理，又把戒指换成餐厅，双重偷换。 借用原文：a silver wedding ring
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：Celebrate his silver wedding anniversary. 里的 silver wedding 拼自录音的 silver wedding ring（银质结婚戒指），但 a silver wedding ring 说的是经理找到的一枚银戒指，根本不是他要庆祝结婚周年；把 silver wedding ring 截成 silver wedding，是诱人的原词陷阱。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（decided to replace the wooden deck ↔ Replace the restaurant's wooden deck. 几乎同表述，仅补出所属）

questions.evidenceText: Recently, the restaurant manager Ryan Krivoy decided to replace the wooden deck and he found an old gold coin, some $100 bills and a silver wedding ring while replacing the deck.

questions.stem: What did the waitress do about the recovered ring?

options.text: She sold it for two thousand dollars.
She took it to the restaurant manager.
She posted its picture on Facebook.
She returned it to its owner right away.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：The restaurant waitress Sasha Formica posted a picture of the ring on Facebook.信号：主语正是 waitress、动作直接针对 ring 。The restaurant waitress Sasha Formica posted a picture of the ring on Facebook. 这…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：She sold it for two thousand dollars. 里的两千美元搬自录音结尾 the gold coin was very rare. It was from 1855 and worth as much as $2,000，但这金额是说那枚稀有金币值两千美元、并非服务员把戒指卖了两千；既盗用了金额数字，又把对象从金币偷换成戒指，是原词陷阱加偷换概念。 借用原文：The restaurant mailed the ring back to the happy couple.
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：She took it to the restaurant manager. 说服务员把戒指交给经理，但录音里其实是经理先发现戒指 he found... a silver wedding ring、服务员再去发照片，戒指并非由服务员上交经理；这是个原文没发生、还把人物关系方向弄反的干扰项。
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：She returned it to its owner right away. 借了录音里确有的归还戒指情节，但还戒指的是餐厅而非服务员 The restaurant mailed the ring back to the happy couple.，而且是失主三天后来认领 Three days later, the happy wife called to claim the ring 才寄还，并非 right away（立刻）；张冠李戴加篡改时间。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（posted a picture of the ring on Facebook ↔ She posted its picture on Facebook. 几乎原句，仅用 its 回指 ring）

questions.evidenceText: The restaurant waitress Sasha Formica posted a picture of the ring on Facebook.

transcript.text: W: I can't believe that duck hunting is still legal in so many parts of the world. The scientific evidence from countries like Australia, Canada and the USA clearly indicates a decline in the birds' numbers.
transcript.zh: W: 我真不敢相信在世界上这么多地方猎鸭仍然是合法的。来自澳大利亚、加拿大和美国等国家的科学证据清楚地表明这些鸟类的数量正在下降。

transcript.text: M: But can anyone be sure if the decline is really caused by the hunting or by climate change?
transcript.zh: M: 但是有人能确定这种下降真的是由狩猎引起的还是由气候变化引起的吗?

transcript.text: W: It's caused by both in fact. We see more droughts in countries like Australia. Ducks are birds that feed and breed in areas where there is a lot of water, but their habitats have been shrinking in recent decades because of the droughts.
transcript.zh: W: 实际上两者都有影响。我们在澳大利亚这样的国家看到更多的干旱。鸭子是在有大量水源的地区觅食和繁殖的鸟类,但近几十年来由于干旱,它们的栖息地一直在缩小。

transcript.text: M: And I guess with fewer places to inhabit, they concentrate in greater numbers in few areas, which surely makes them easier targets for the hunters.
transcript.zh: M: 我猜随着可居住的地方越来越少,它们会更集中地聚集在少数几个区域,这肯定让它们更容易成为猎人的目标。

transcript.text: W: It does. My grandfather was a duck hunter. He told me hunting ducks and geese began in the 19th century. They were easily found and a plentifully available food source in farming areas, especially for poor immigrants.
transcript.zh: W: 确实如此。我祖父曾是个猎鸭人。他告诉我猎鸭和猎鹅始于19世纪。在农业地区它们很容易找到,是充足的食物来源,尤其对贫穷的移民来说。

transcript.text: M: What do they use for hunting during that period?
transcript.zh: M: 那个时期他们用什么来狩猎?

transcript.text: W: They use new types of guns, and birds could easily be shot down in flight. And in such great numbers, their commercial hunting of ducks and geese became an industry. Yet, there's no commercial farming of these birds nowadays. Their meat is hardly eaten in Western countries.
transcript.zh: W: 他们使用新型枪支,鸟类在飞行中很容易被射下来。而且数量如此之多,对鸭子和鹅的商业狩猎成了一个产业。然而,现在已经没有这些鸟类的商业养殖了。在西方国家几乎没人吃它们的肉。

transcript.text: M: No, duck hunting seemingly exists as the continuation of a tradition.
transcript.zh: M: 是的,猎鸭似乎只是作为一种传统的延续而存在。

transcript.text: W: Well, ducks have never been popular with farmers like my grandfather anyway because they sometimes destroy crops. In fact, farmers used to poison them in large numbers.
transcript.zh: W: 其实,鸭子从来都不受像我祖父这样的农民欢迎,因为它们有时会破坏庄稼。事实上,农民过去常常大量毒杀它们。

transcript.text: M: That somehow doesn't surprise me. Nobody places much value on the lives of these poor birds or on their meat.

transcript.text: Homework is an important part of schooling, but the purposes of giving children homework will change as they grow older. At the primary level, the main aim is to cultivate good habits, like learning to plan and exercising self-discipline. During the secondary school years, extending what is learned at school is positively related to academic achievement, so the content of homework becomes more important.
transcript.zh: 家庭作业是学校教育的重要组成部分,但给孩子布置作业的目的会随着他们年龄的增长而改变。在小学阶段,主要目的是培养良好的习惯,比如学会计划和锻炼自律。在中学阶段,拓展在学校学到的知识与学业成绩呈正相关,因此作业的内容变得更加重要。

transcript.text: So how can you help your child do their best?
transcript.zh: 那么你如何帮助孩子做到最好呢?

transcript.text: Creating an ideal working environment will make it easier for them to get down to their assignments quickly. Make sure it's free of distractions, and for primary school children at least somewhere near you, so you can answer questions and offer encouragement.
transcript.zh: 创造一个理想的学习环境会让他们更容易快速投入作业。确保环境没有干扰,至少对小学生来说要在你附近的某个地方,这样你就能回答问题并给予鼓励。

transcript.text: You probably have to help younger children plan their session, but it's important that by the end of primary school it's second nature. Get them to tell you everything they have to do. Then encourage them to establish an order in which they do work.
transcript.zh: 你可能需要帮助年幼的孩子规划他们的学习时段,但重要的是到小学毕业时这应该成为自然而然的事情。让他们告诉你所有需要做的事情,然后鼓励他们确定完成作业的顺序。

transcript.text: When there are several different assignments, make sure they begin with one they enjoy, so it seems easy to get started. It's best to take on the most difficult task second once they're settled, but before they get tired.
transcript.zh: 当有几项不同的作业时,确保他们从喜欢的作业开始,这样看起来容易上手。最好在他们进入状态后、但还没感到疲倦之前,第二个处理最难的任务。

transcript.text: If older children have more than an hour of homework, encourage them to schedule a short break to stretch.
transcript.zh: 如果年龄较大的孩子有超过一小时的作业,鼓励他们安排一个短暂的休息时间来伸展身体。

transcript.text: If you encourage them to tell you what they've learned, they'll absorb the information more deeply and remember it more readily.
transcript.zh: 如果你鼓励他们告诉你学到了什么,他们会更深入地吸收信息并更容易记住它。

transcript.text: Workers at Mexican oil company will receive a healthy incentive of almost $300 a year if they meet certain body weight standards. To qualify for the bonus, they must maintain a healthy weight. For those who are overweight or obese, they could receive the bonus if they reduce their weight by 10% during the year.
transcript.zh: 墨西哥石油公司的员工如果达到特定体重标准，将获得每年近300美元的丰厚奖励。要获得这项奖金，他们必须保持健康体重。对于超重或肥胖的员工,如果在一年内减重10%,也可以获得该奖金。

transcript.text: Some applaud the policy as fair, because it rewards both the individuals who maintain a healthy weight and those who are working towards achieving it.
transcript.zh: 一些人赞扬这项政策公平合理,因为它既奖励保持健康体重的个人,也奖励那些正在努力实现这一目标的人。

transcript.text: But critics say the policy contradicts recommendations by many health experts, who warn that a person's weight is influenced by genetic and environmental factors. That means weight can be hard for individuals to control, which makes the bonus unfair.
transcript.zh: 但批评者表示,这项政策与许多健康专家的建议相矛盾,这些专家警告说,一个人的体重受遗传和环境因素的影响。这意味着体重对个人来说很难控制,这使得这项奖金不公平。

transcript.text: Some experts say the policy is inconsistent with the science of what we know about body weight regulation. These experts argue that focusing on wage is the wrong approach. A more productive method of encouraging health among employees is to promote healthy behaviors. For example, companies can give workers gym memberships, or encourage participation in lectures on healthy eating and living. They can also reduce sweets and provide healthier snacks in the office and healthier meals at the company canteen. Or they can give employees more time during their lunch break to exercise. These are much better and much more productive ways for companies to move forward on their employees' wellbeing.
transcript.zh: 一些专家表示,这项政策与我们关于体重调节的科学知识不一致。这些专家认为,关注体重是错误的方法。鼓励员工健康的更有效方法是促进健康行为。例如,公司可以为员工提供健身房会员资格,或鼓励参加有关健康饮食和生活的讲座。他们还可以减少甜食,在办公室提供更健康的零食,在公司食堂提供更健康的餐食。或者他们可以在午休时间给员工更多时间锻炼。这些都是公司在员工福祉方面前进的更好、更有效的方式。

transcript.text: Campaigners have warned that the British government is not doing enough to prevent left-handed pupils from falling behind their peers. They claim that thousands of children are still being "penalized" for being left-handed. This is due to a lack of action from ministers, who've failed to take any meaningful action for years.
transcript.zh: 活动人士警告称,英国政府在防止左撇子学生落后于同龄人方面做得不够。他们声称,成千上万的儿童仍因左撇子而受到"惩罚"。这是由于部长们缺乏行动,多年来未能采取任何有意义的措施。

transcript.text: It is feared that a failure to address early-year challenges, such as poor handwriting, leads to much more serious problems down the line—with these pupils facing reduced career prospects.
transcript.zh: 人们担心,如果不能解决早期阶段的挑战,例如书写能力差,会导致后续出现更严重的问题——这些学生将面临职业前景受限的困境。

transcript.text: Studies in recent years show that left-handed children are more likely to suffer with learning difficulties and their scores are lower on IQ tests.
transcript.zh: 近年来的研究表明,左撇子儿童更容易出现学习困难,他们在智商测试中的得分也较低。

transcript.text: Campaigners feel it's strange that children in British schools are penalized because they happen to be left-handed. They don't understand why successive governments have failed to act on this. They want the department of education to record which children are left-handed and what their educational attainments are, since they make up some 10% of the population.
transcript.zh: 活动人士认为奇怪的是,英国学校的儿童会因为恰好是左撇子而受到惩罚。他们不理解为什么历届政府都未能就此采取行动。他们希望教育部记录哪些儿童是左撇子以及他们的学业成绩如何,因为左撇子占人口的约10%。

transcript.text: In early-year education, left-handed children are struggling and making a mess of their handwriting. Educators don't know how to deal with this. In many cases, there is no active help and a lack of teacher training. Campaigners point out that a high percentage of the prison population is left-handed. They say that these prison numbers are unusually high and ask why it is the case.
transcript.zh: 在早期教育中,左撇子儿童很吃力,把字写得一团糟。教育工作者不知道如何应对这一问题。在许多情况下,没有积极的帮助,也缺乏教师培训。活动人士指出,监狱人口中左撇子的比例很高。他们说这些监狱数字异常高,并询问为什么会出现这种情况。

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: "I used to work very hard. I love to create things, grow them and solve problems," said Meng Li, a successful app developer in San Francisco. "I didn't really care about my mind and my body until they decided to go on strike."

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Ms. Li said her stress led to sleeplessness. When she did sleep, she experienced "problem-solving dreams," which left her feeling unrested when she woke up. "After I became a first-time mother, I quickly realized I was so busy caring for other people and work that I felt like I'd lost myself," she said.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: It's a common story—one we frequently ridicule and readily dismiss, for example, by claiming that women tend to complain more than men, despite the growing sum of research that underlines the problem. Women are twice as likely to suffer from severe stress and anxiety as men, according to a 2016 study published in The Journal of Brain & Behavior. The American Psychological Association reports a gender gap year after year showing that women consistently report higher stress levels. Clearly, a stress gap exists.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: "The difference is not really news to me, as a clinical psychologist," said Erin Joyce, a women and couples therapist in Los Angeles. "It's been well documented in extensive research over the years that prevalence rates for the majority of the anxiety disorders are higher in women than men." Some people may argue that this is merely reported data, and they say many men feel the same pressures as women in terms of fulfilling responsibilities at work and home. In other words, we're all really, really stressed.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: "The difference, however, is in the nature and scope of these responsibilities in the home environment in particular," Dr. Joyce said. For example, the United Nations reported that women do nearly three times as much unpaid domestic work as men. The problem is, housework is often overlooked as work, even though it is often as laborious (or in some cases, more so) as any paid job. As the scholar Silvia Federici put it in 1975, the unpaid nature of domestic work reinforces the assumption that "housework is not work, thus preventing women from struggling against it."

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: It's not just inside the home, though. Research from Nova Southeastern University found that female managers were more likely than male managers to display "surface acting," or forcing emotions that are not wholly felt. "They expressed optimism, calmness and sympathy even when these were not the emotions that they were actually feeling," the study said.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Surface acting is a prime example of "emotional labor," a concept that the writer Jess Zimmerman made familiar in a 2015 essay. The essay sparked a massive thread on the internet community blog MetaFilter. Hundreds of women spoke up about their own experience with emotional labor: the duties that are expected of them, but go unnoticed. These invisible duties become apparent only when you don't do them. Like domestic labor, emotional labor is generally dismissed and not labeled work. But research shows it can be just as exhausting as paid work. Emotional labor can lead to difficulty in sleeping and family conflict. Sure, circumstantial stress, like losing a job, may lead to these same issues. But emotional labor is not circumstantial. It's an enduring responsibility based on the socialized gender role of women.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Like Ms. Li, many women try to manage the added stress to reach what Dr. Joyce said was an unattainable ideal. "Some professional women aim to do it all. They want to reach the top of the corporate ladder and fly like supermom," she said. When women don't reach this ideal, they feel guilty; and even more stressed. After her own struggle with this, Ms. Li took a step back and used her experience to build Sanity & Self, a self-care app and platform for overworked women. "The realizations I had in that process helped me gain insights and ultimately got me ready to integrate self-care into my daily life," she said.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: The stress problem extends beyond mental health when you consider the link between stress, anxiety and heart health. Worse, most of what we know about heart disease comes from studies involving men. However, "there are many reasons to think that it's different in women," Harvard Medical School reported. For example, women are more likely to experience disturbed sleep, anxiety and unusual fatigue before a heart attack. Stress is so normalized that it is easy for women to shrug off those symptoms as simply the consequences of stress. Many women also do not experience chest pain before a heart attack the way men do, which leads to fewer women discovering problematic heart issues. Harvard reports that women are "much more likely than men to die within a year of having a heart attack" and "many women say their physicians sometimes don't even recognize the symptoms."

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: The good news is, women are more likely than men to take charge of their stress and manage it, the American Psychological Association reports. The concept of self-care, at its core, is quite simple. "The basics of adequate sleep, healthy diet and exercise are a good place to start," Dr. Joyce said. "Support from trusted relationships is vital. This includes professional support from various health and wellness providers if stress is becoming increasingly overwhelming."

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Disconnecting from work and home responsibilities is also obviously important. But it's much easier said than done. It is important to understand what causes your stress in the first place. "Get really specific with what's stressing you out," Ms. Li said. "We often chalk up our stress to broad experiences like work. But work stress can take many different forms. Is a colleague being disrespectful of your time? Is a boss undermining your day-to-day control over decision making? These are different causes of stress and can benefit from different kinds of self-care."

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: Ideally, your spouse or partner will be supportive, rather than dismissive, of your stress. It is important to talk through these issues before they come to a head. "Women working outside of the home should make an effort to have a conscious conversation with their partners about more equitable sharing of household and family responsibilities," Dr. Joyce said.
